kinds.does: How many items leave the station each week.
How long an item waits before the station starts on it.
How long the station works on an item.
The share of items the station sends back or has to redo.
How many items stand at the station at the end of the period, and how old the oldest is.
The hours items spend at the station, wait and work together. The constraint is the station with the most.
Numbers that fit none of the five.

units.does: Items per week: the count in the period divided by the length of the period in weeks.
Hours of wall-clock time. Nights and weekends count.
A share between 0 and 1. 0.25 is 25 percent.
A plain count at one moment.

rules: A definition says "the period". For the value of a metric that is the whole window of the report, 13 weeks unless asked otherwise. For one point of its history it is one week.

A station's numbers are counted when they happen, not when the change merges. A wait counts in the period it ended, and work in the period the item left the station. A change that waited four weeks for review and got it this week counts this week, at the review station, whether or not it has merged yet.
The numbers about the whole line are measured over the changes merged in the period.
Queue numbers are not measured over a period. They are the state at the end of it.
A median, a percentile or a share drawn from fewer than 5 items is still reported, and marked thin. No trend is called on a thin value.
Every time is wall-clock time. Nights and weekends count, because the work waits through them.
Changes by automation, such as dependency bumps and release bots, are reported as their own class and are left out of every number about the whole line.
A metric id never changes meaning. When a definition has to change, the metric gets a new id and the old one stays or is removed in a new contract version.

stations.name: Spec
stations.does: A ticket is written and waits for someone to start on it.
stations.leaves: Work starts: the ticket first moves to a started state, or its first linked change is opened, whichever comes first.
stations.why: A backlog holds tickets on purpose, often for months. Counting that as waiting would name spec the constraint in every repository.

not_observable.held: Spec is left out of the constraint, so its hours are not added up.
not_observable.work: Writing a ticket leaves no start time.

stations.name: Code
stations.arrives: The first commit of the change is written or the change is opened, whichever is earlier.
stations.leaves: The change is marked ready for review. A change opened ready leaves when it is opened.

not_observable.wait: Code has no queue of its own. A ticket waiting for someone to start waits at spec.

stations.name: CI
stations.does: The checks run on each push to a change. One CI round is every run on one commit of a change.
stations.arrives: The first run on the commit is created.
stations.leaves: The last run on the commit finishes.

not_observable.queue: A CI round lasts minutes. A count of rounds in flight at the end of a week says nothing about the week.

stations.name: Verify
stations.does: The change is proved on a running environment before it merges.
stations.arrives: A commit of the change is deployed to an environment that is not production.

not_observable.queue: Nothing records that a change is waiting for an environment.

stations.name: Review
stations.does: Another person reads the change and approves it or sends it back.
stations.arrives: The change is marked ready for review.
stations.leaves: The last approval before the merge. A change that merges after a review with no approval leaves at the merge. A change nobody else reviewed skips the station.

stations.name: Merge
stations.does: The approved change lands on the main branch.
stations.arrives: The change leaves review. A change nobody else reviewed arrives when it is marked ready for review.

not_observable.work: A merge is one click. It has no start time apart from its end.

stations.name: Release
stations.leaves: The first production deploy that holds it. A change merged before the first production deploy in the store is not counted.

metrics.name: Tickets started
metrics.definition: Tickets that work started on in the period. Work starts when the ticket first moves to a started state or its first linked change is opened, whichever comes first. The count is divided by the length of the period in weeks.

metrics.name: Wait for work to start, median
metrics.definition: Hours from a ticket leaving the backlog to work starting on it, over the tickets that work started on in the period. A ticket leaves the backlog the first time it is in a state that is not triage or backlog. A GitHub issue has no backlog, so it waits from when it was created. The median.

metrics.name: Wait for work to start, 90th percentile
metrics.definition: Hours from a ticket leaving the backlog to work starting on it, over the tickets that work started on in the period. A ticket leaves the backlog the first time it is in a state that is not triage or backlog. A GitHub issue has no backlog, so it waits from when it was created. The 90th percentile: one item in ten waited longer.

metrics.name: Tickets reopened
metrics.definition: Share of the tickets finished in the period that had been finished before and were opened again.

metrics.name: Tickets not started
metrics.definition: Tickets that are open, out of the backlog and that nobody has started, at the end of the period. Tickets in triage or the backlog are not waiting for the line, and cancelled tickets are left out.

metrics.name: Tickets not started, age of the oldest
metrics.definition: Hours since it left the backlog, for the item that has stood longest in this queue at the end of the period. Tickets that are open, out of the backlog and that nobody has started, at the end of the period. Tickets in triage or the backlog are not waiting for the line, and cancelled tickets are left out.

metrics.name: PRs made ready
metrics.definition: Changes marked ready for review in the period. A change opened ready counts when it is opened. The count is divided by the length of the period in weeks.

metrics.name: Time to write a PR, median
metrics.definition: Hours from the start of a change to it being marked ready for review, over the changes marked ready in the period. The start is the first commit or the opening of the change, whichever is earlier. Merge commits, and commits written more than 90 days before the change was opened, do not count: they are history the change carries, or a wrong date. The median.

metrics.name: Time to write a PR, 90th percentile
metrics.definition: Hours from the start of a change to it being marked ready for review, over the changes marked ready in the period. The start is the first commit or the opening of the change, whichever is earlier. Merge commits, and commits written more than 90 days before the change was opened, do not count: they are history the change carries, or a wrong date. The 90th percentile: one item in ten took longer.

metrics.name: PRs abandoned
metrics.definition: Share of the changes closed in the period that were closed without merging.

metrics.name: PRs in draft
metrics.definition: Changes that are open and still a draft at the end of the period.

metrics.name: PRs in draft, age of the oldest
metrics.definition: Hours since it was opened, for the item that has stood longest in this queue at the end of the period. Changes that are open and still a draft at the end of the period.

metrics.name: Hours a week held at code
metrics.definition: Hours the items that left the code station in the period spent there, wait and work together, per week. Each item is capped at the 90th percentile of the station, so one item that sat for months cannot decide the total. Time with a CI run in flight is counted at ci and taken out of the station the change stood at, so no hour is counted twice.

metrics.name: Share of the line's time held at code
metrics.definition: The held hours of the code station divided by the held hours of every station that counts for the constraint. The station with the largest share is the constraint.

metrics.name: CI rounds
metrics.definition: CI rounds that finished in the period. A CI round is every run on one commit of a change. The runs a merge queue starts for a change are a round of their own. Skipped and cancelled runs are left out. The count is divided by the length of the period in weeks.

metrics.name: Wait for a runner, median
metrics.definition: Hours from the first run of a CI round being created to the first run starting, over the rounds that finished in the period. The median.

metrics.name: Wait for a runner, 90th percentile
metrics.definition: Hours from the first run of a CI round being created to the first run starting, over the rounds that finished in the period. The 90th percentile: one item in ten waited longer.

metrics.name: CI round time, median
metrics.definition: Hours with at least one run in flight, from the first run of a CI round starting to the last one finishing, over the rounds that finished in the period. The median.

metrics.name: CI round time, 90th percentile
metrics.definition: Hours with at least one run in flight, from the first run of a CI round starting to the last one finishing, over the rounds that finished in the period. The 90th percentile: one item in ten took longer.

metrics.name: CI rounds that failed
metrics.definition: Share of the CI rounds finished in the period in which a run failed, timed out or was run again.

metrics.name: Hours a week held at ci
metrics.definition: Hours the items that left the ci station in the period spent there, wait and work together, per week. Each item is capped at the 90th percentile of the station, so one item that sat for months cannot decide the total. Time with a CI run in flight is counted at ci and taken out of the station the change stood at, so no hour is counted twice.

metrics.name: Share of the line's time held at ci
metrics.definition: The held hours of the ci station divided by the held hours of every station that counts for the constraint. The station with the largest share is the constraint.

metrics.name: PRs verified
metrics.definition: Changes whose first deployment to an environment that is not production reported success in the period. The count is divided by the length of the period in weeks.

metrics.name: Wait for an environment, median
metrics.definition: Hours from a commit of a change being written to its deployment to an environment that is not production being created, over the deployments created in the period. The median.

metrics.name: Wait for an environment, 90th percentile
metrics.definition: Hours from a commit of a change being written to its deployment to an environment that is not production being created, over the deployments created in the period. The 90th percentile: one item in ten waited longer.

metrics.name: Time to bring the PR up, median
metrics.definition: Hours from such a deployment being created to it reporting success, over the deployments that reported success in the period. The median.

metrics.name: Time to bring the PR up, 90th percentile
metrics.definition: Hours from such a deployment being created to it reporting success, over the deployments that reported success in the period. The 90th percentile: one item in ten took longer.

metrics.name: Verify deployments that failed
metrics.definition: Share of the deployments of changes to an environment that is not production, finished in the period, that reported a failure or an error.

metrics.name: Hours a week held at verify
metrics.definition: Hours the items that left the verify station in the period spent there, wait and work together, per week. Each item is capped at the 90th percentile of the station, so one item that sat for months cannot decide the total. Time with a CI run in flight is counted at ci and taken out of the station the change stood at, so no hour is counted twice.

metrics.name: Share of the line's time held at verify
metrics.definition: The held hours of the verify station divided by the held hours of every station that counts for the constraint. The station with the largest share is the constraint.

metrics.name: PRs reviewed
metrics.definition: Merged changes that left review in the period. A change leaves review at its last approval before the merge, or at the merge when it was reviewed and never approved. A review counts when a person other than the author wrote it. Reviews by bots and by the author do not count. The count is divided by the length of the period in weeks.

metrics.name: Wait for first review, median
metrics.definition: Hours from a change being marked ready for review to its first review, over the changes that got their first review in the period. A review that lands while the change is a draft gives a wait of zero. A review counts when a person other than the author wrote it. Reviews by bots and by the author do not count. The median.

metrics.name: Wait for first review, 90th percentile
metrics.definition: Hours from a change being marked ready for review to its first review, over the changes that got their first review in the period. A review that lands while the change is a draft gives a wait of zero. A review counts when a person other than the author wrote it. Reviews by bots and by the author do not count. The 90th percentile: one item in ten waited longer.

metrics.name: First review to approval, median
metrics.definition: Hours from the first review of a change to it leaving review, over the merged changes that left review in the period. A review counts when a person other than the author wrote it. Reviews by bots and by the author do not count. The median.

metrics.name: First review to approval, 90th percentile
metrics.definition: Hours from the first review of a change to it leaving review, over the merged changes that left review in the period. A review counts when a person other than the author wrote it. Reviews by bots and by the author do not count. The 90th percentile: one item in ten took longer.

metrics.name: PRs sent back in review
metrics.definition: Share of the merged changes that left review in the period on which a reviewer requested changes, or which got a new commit after the first review. Merge commits do not count.

metrics.name: PRs waiting for first review
metrics.definition: Changes that are open, ready for review and without a review at the end of the period. A review counts when a person other than the author wrote it. Reviews by bots and by the author do not count.

metrics.name: PRs waiting for first review, age of the oldest
metrics.definition: Hours since it was marked ready for review, for the item that has stood longest in this queue at the end of the period. Changes that are open, ready for review and without a review at the end of the period. A review counts when a person other than the author wrote it. Reviews by bots and by the author do not count.

metrics.name: Hours a week held at review
metrics.definition: Hours the items that left the review station in the period spent there, wait and work together, per week. Each item is capped at the 90th percentile of the station, so one item that sat for months cannot decide the total. Time with a CI run in flight is counted at ci and taken out of the station the change stood at, so no hour is counted twice.

metrics.name: Share of the line's time held at review
metrics.definition: The held hours of the review station divided by the held hours of every station that counts for the constraint. The station with the largest share is the constraint.

metrics.name: PRs merged with no review
metrics.definition: Share of the changes merged in the period that no other person reviewed before the merge. A review counts when a person other than the author wrote it. Reviews by bots and by the author do not count.

metrics.name: PRs merged
metrics.definition: Changes merged in the period. The count is divided by the length of the period in weeks.

metrics.name: Wait to merge, median
metrics.definition: Hours from a change arriving at merge to it merging, over the changes merged in the period. A change arrives when it leaves review. A change nobody else reviewed arrives when it is marked ready for review. The median.

metrics.name: Wait to merge, 90th percentile
metrics.definition: Hours from a change arriving at merge to it merging, over the changes merged in the period. A change arrives when it leaves review. A change nobody else reviewed arrives when it is marked ready for review. The 90th percentile: one item in ten waited longer.

metrics.name: Merges reverted
metrics.definition: Share of the changes merged in the period that a later change reverted. A change reverts another when its description says so in the words the code host writes for a revert.

metrics.name: PRs approved and not merged
metrics.definition: Changes that are open and approved at the end of the period, with no request for changes after the last approval.

metrics.name: PRs approved and not merged, age of the oldest
metrics.definition: Hours since its last approval, for the item that has stood longest in this queue at the end of the period. Changes that are open and approved at the end of the period, with no request for changes after the last approval.

metrics.name: Hours a week held at merge
metrics.definition: Hours the items that left the merge station in the period spent there, wait and work together, per week. Each item is capped at the 90th percentile of the station, so one item that sat for months cannot decide the total. Time with a CI run in flight is counted at ci and taken out of the station the change stood at, so no hour is counted twice.

metrics.name: Share of the line's time held at merge
metrics.definition: The held hours of the merge station divided by the held hours of every station that counts for the constraint. The station with the largest share is the constraint.

metrics.name: PRs released
metrics.definition: Merged changes that reached production in the period. A production deploy of the commit a merge left on its branch holds the changes merged into that branch up to that merge. Of any other deploy only the time is known, and it is taken to hold the changes merged before it started. The count is divided by the length of the period in weeks.

metrics.name: Wait for a release, median
metrics.definition: Hours from a change merging to the start of the production deploy that shipped it, over the changes that reached production in the period. A production deploy of the commit a merge left on its branch holds the changes merged into that branch up to that merge. Of any other deploy only the time is known, and it is taken to hold the changes merged before it started. The median.

metrics.name: Wait for a release, 90th percentile
metrics.definition: Hours from a change merging to the start of the production deploy that shipped it, over the changes that reached production in the period. A production deploy of the commit a merge left on its branch holds the changes merged into that branch up to that merge. Of any other deploy only the time is known, and it is taken to hold the changes merged before it started. The 90th percentile: one item in ten waited longer.

metrics.name: Deploy time, median
metrics.definition: Hours from a production deploy being created to it reporting success, over the production deploys that reported success in the period. The median.

metrics.name: Deploy time, 90th percentile
metrics.definition: Hours from a production deploy being created to it reporting success, over the production deploys that reported success in the period. The 90th percentile: one item in ten took longer.

metrics.name: Deploys that failed
metrics.definition: Share of the production deploys finished in the period that reported a failure or an error.

metrics.name: PRs merged and not released
metrics.definition: Changes that are merged and that no production deploy has followed, at the end of the period.

metrics.name: PRs merged and not released, age of the oldest
metrics.definition: Hours since it merged, for the item that has stood longest in this queue at the end of the period. Changes that are merged and that no production deploy has followed, at the end of the period.

metrics.name: Hours a week held at release
metrics.definition: Hours the items that left the release station in the period spent there, wait and work together, per week. Each item is capped at the 90th percentile of the station, so one item that sat for months cannot decide the total. Time with a CI run in flight is counted at ci and taken out of the station the change stood at, so no hour is counted twice.

metrics.name: Share of the line's time held at release
metrics.definition: The held hours of the release station divided by the held hours of every station that counts for the constraint. The station with the largest share is the constraint.

metrics.name: Production deploys
metrics.definition: Production deploys created in the period, per week. A deploy is a deployment to an environment whose name says production, or a published release when the repository has no such deployment.

metrics.name: PRs merged
metrics.definition: Changes merged in the period, per week. For the whole line this counts changes by agents and by people. Automation is left out.

metrics.name: Open to merge, median
metrics.definition: Hours from a change being opened to it merging, over the changes merged in the period. The median.

metrics.name: Open to merge, 90th percentile
metrics.definition: Hours from a change being opened to it merging, over the changes merged in the period. The 90th percentile: one change in ten took longer.

metrics.name: Start to production, median
metrics.definition: Hours from the start of a change to the production deploy that shipped it, over the changes that reached production in the period. The start is the first commit or the opening of the change, whichever is earlier. Merge commits, and commits written more than 90 days before the change was opened, do not count: they are history the change carries, or a wrong date. The median. A production deploy of the commit a merge left on its branch holds the changes merged into that branch up to that merge. Of any other deploy only the time is known, and it is taken to hold the changes merged before it started.

metrics.name: Disclosed agent share
metrics.definition: Changes by agents divided by changes by agents and by people, over the changes merged in the period. Automation is left out of both sides. It is a floor: an agent that leaves no trace counts as a person.

metrics.name: Lines changed, median
metrics.definition: Lines added plus lines deleted, over the changes merged in the period. The median.

recommendation_rules.title: Get changes ready for review sooner
recommendation_rules.fires: The station is the constraint. Or it holds an item at least 25 percent longer than in its own best four weeks, and running at that pace would give back at least 5 percent of the hours changes are held before the merge.
recommendation_rules.sized: The mean hours an item is held at the station now, less the same mean in the station's best four weeks, times the items that leave the station in a week. Each item is capped at the 90th percentile of the items it is averaged with.

recommendation_rules.title: Make CI rounds shorter
recommendation_rules.fires: The station is the constraint. Or it holds an item at least 25 percent longer than in its own best four weeks, and running at that pace would give back at least 5 percent of the hours changes are held before the merge.
recommendation_rules.sized: The mean hours an item is held at the station now, less the same mean in the station's best four weeks, times the items that leave the station in a week. Each item is capped at the 90th percentile of the items it is averaged with.

recommendation_rules.title: Bring changes up on an environment faster
recommendation_rules.fires: The station is the constraint. Or it holds an item at least 25 percent longer than in its own best four weeks, and running at that pace would give back at least 5 percent of the hours changes are held before the merge.
recommendation_rules.sized: The mean hours an item is held at the station now, less the same mean in the station's best four weeks, times the items that leave the station in a week. Each item is capped at the 90th percentile of the items it is averaged with.

recommendation_rules.title: Cut the wait for review
recommendation_rules.fires: The station is the constraint. Or it holds an item at least 25 percent longer than in its own best four weeks, and running at that pace would give back at least 5 percent of the hours changes are held before the merge.
recommendation_rules.sized: The mean hours an item is held at the station now, less the same mean in the station's best four weeks, times the items that leave the station in a week. Each item is capped at the 90th percentile of the items it is averaged with.

recommendation_rules.title: Merge finished changes sooner
recommendation_rules.fires: The station is the constraint. Or it holds an item at least 25 percent longer than in its own best four weeks, and running at that pace would give back at least 5 percent of the hours changes are held before the merge.
recommendation_rules.sized: The mean hours an item is held at the station now, less the same mean in the station's best four weeks, times the items that leave the station in a week. Each item is capped at the 90th percentile of the items it is averaged with.

recommendation_rules.title: Release more often
recommendation_rules.fires: The station is the constraint. Or it holds an item at least 25 percent longer than in its own best four weeks, and running at that pace would give back at least 5 percent of the hours changes are held on the whole line.
recommendation_rules.sized: The mean hours an item is held at the station now, less the same mean in the station's best four weeks, times the items that leave the station in a week. Each item is capped at the 90th percentile of the items it is averaged with.

recommendation_rules.title: Prove changes on a running environment before they merge
recommendation_rules.fires: The verify station is not connected, and at least 50 percent of the changes merged in the window had no review by another person.

recommendation_rules.title: Cut the share of CI rounds that fail
recommendation_rules.fires: At least 15 percent of the CI rounds in the window failed, timed out or were run again. The evidence names the workflows whose runs did so most often.
recommendation_rules.sized: The share of failed rounds now, less the share in the best four weeks, times the rounds in a week, times the mean hours a round holds a change.

recommendation_rules.title: Have agents run the checks before they push
recommendation_rules.fires: CI rounds on changes by agents fail at least 5 points more often than rounds on changes by people. Both sides are drawn from at least 5 items.

recommendation_rules.title: Find out why merged changes get reverted
recommendation_rules.fires: At least 5 percent of the changes merged in the window were reverted later, and at least 3 of them.

recommendation_rules.title: Find out why changes are closed without merging
recommendation_rules.fires: At least 20 percent of the changes closed in the window were closed without merging.

recommendation_rules.title: Clear the review queue
recommendation_rules.fires: At least 5 changes wait for a first review at the end of the window, and the trend of the queue is worse: it is longer than at the end of the window before by more than the report calls flat. The rule is silent when no change in the store was ever reviewed by another person.

recommendation_rules.title: Merge the changes that are already approved
recommendation_rules.fires: At least 3 changes have been approved for more than 24 hours and are not merged at the end of the window.

recommendation_rules.title: Finish or close the drafts that stopped moving
recommendation_rules.fires: At least 3 changes have been a draft for more than 14 days at the end of the window.

recommendation_rules.title: Find out why finished tickets are opened again
recommendation_rules.fires: At least 10 percent of the tickets finished in the window had been finished before and were opened again. The share is drawn from at least 5 tickets.

recommendation_rules.title: Close or schedule the tickets nobody has started
recommendation_rules.fires: At least 5 tickets have been open for more than 90 days at the end of the window with no work started on them.

recommendation_rules.title: Write up more work that is ready to start
recommendation_rules.fires: Fewer tickets are open and not started at the end of the window than the line starts in one week. The pace is drawn from at least 5 tickets started in the window.

recommendation_rules.title: Find out why changes by agents wait longer for review
recommendation_rules.fires: The median wait for a first review is at least 1.5 times as long for changes by agents as for changes by people, and at least 1 hour longer. Both sides are drawn from at least 5 items.

recommendation_rules.title: Have agents ship smaller changes
recommendation_rules.fires: The median change by an agent is at least 2 times the size of the median change by a person, and at least 200 lines. Both sides are drawn from at least 5 items.
